title: LLM as judge: model-based evaluation and its limits

videos.script: Some things have no answer key. Is this reply warm? Does it actually answer the question? The tempting fix is to ask another model. {{title}} This lesson builds that judge out of the model you already have, and then measures it. The judge reads a customer message and two replies, and says which one is better. {{judge}} Sixteen pairs carry a person's verdict. The judge agrees on eight of them, and it said b thirteen times. Correct for chance, and kappa comes out at a tenth. {{kappa}} Then you swap the order of the replies. The judge changes its mind on twelve of the sixteen, and it mostly picks whichever reply it read second. Ask it the identical question a second time, at temperature zero, and one verdict changes anyway. {{swap}} Four verdicts survive the swap. In all four the judge chose the longer reply. {{length}} Last, a question about this platform. It grades every exercise you answer, and it never uses a model to do it. You will see exactly why. {{platform}} By the end you know where a judge helps, and where it must never have the last word. {{close}}
